title: Blocker: MessagePort for Cross-Realm Stream Transfer
description:
Implement MessagePort to enable cross-realm stream transfer via postMessage().

## Problem

Streams can be transferred between realms (e.g., main thread ↔ worker) using structured clone. This requires MessagePort for communication between the transferred stream and its original controller.

Currently setupCrossRealmTransformReadable() and setupCrossRealmTransformWritable() return NotImplemented.

## Affected Files

- src/streams/internal/cross_realm_transform.zig (Lines 49-59, 84-96, 133, 208, 229)
- src/streams/internal/message_port.zig

## Required MessagePort API

1. **Core MessagePort**
   - postMessage(message, transfer) - Send message
   - start() - Enable message queue
   - close() - Close port
   - onmessage handler
   - onmessageerror handler

2. **Message Protocol (for streams)**
   - {type: "chunk", value: <chunk>} - Data chunk
   - {type: "close"} - Stream closed
   - {type: "error", value: <error>} - Stream errored
   - {type: "pull"} - Backpressure signal

3. **Port Management**
   - MessageChannel() - Create entangled port pair
   - disentangle(port) - Break port connection

## Implementation Approach

1. Implement MessagePort interface per HTML spec
2. Add structured clone for stream transfer
3. Implement message protocol in cross_realm_transform.zig
4. Wire up event handlers for message types

## Success Criteria

- [ ] MessagePort.postMessage() works
- [ ] MessageChannel creates entangled ports
- [ ] Stream chunks flow through ports
- [ ] Backpressure signals propagate
- [ ] Errors propagate correctly
- [ ] Ports clean up on stream close

## Estimated Effort

5-7 days (MessagePort is a significant component)

## Dependencies

- DOM Events (for onmessage/onmessageerror)
- Structured Clone algorithm
- HTML event loop integration

## Spec References

- HTML § MessagePort
- HTML § Structured Clone
- WHATWG Streams § 4.11.10 SetUpCrossRealmTransformReadable
- WHATWG Streams § 4.11.11 SetUpCrossRealmTransformWritable

title: Fixed: Memory leak in AllowSharedBufferSource V8 conversion
description:
## Problem

The `convertAllowSharedBufferSource\(\)` function in `src/runtime/engines/v8/conversions.zig` was allocating memory that was never freed:
1. Created an `ArrayBuffer` struct via `allocator.create\(\)`
2. Allocated data buffer via `allocator.alloc\(u8, byte_length\)`
3. Copied data from V8 TypedArray into the new buffer

These allocations were never freed after `TextDecoder.decode\(\)` finished.

## Root Cause

The conversion used one allocator \(isolate allocator\) but the cleanup attempted to use a different allocator \(`instance.ctx.allocator`\), causing segfaults when trying to free.

## Solution

Changed the conversion to use a non-owning `byte_slice` variant instead of allocating:

1. Added `byte_slice: []const u8` variant to `AllowSharedBufferSource` union
2. Modified `convertAllowSharedBufferSource\(\)` to return a direct view into the V8 buffer
3. Added `freeBufferSource\(\)` helper that handles cleanup for all variants \(no-op for byte_slice\)

This approach is:
- **Memory safe**: No allocations to leak
- **Faster**: Zero-copy view into V8 buffer
- **Simpler**: No allocator tracking needed
- **Safe**: V8 buffer remains valid during synchronous decode call

## Files Changed

- `src/runtime/engines/v8/conversions.zig` - Changed to use byte_slice
- `src/webidl/types/buffer_sources.zig` - Added byte_slice variant
- `src/webidl/impls/TextDecoder.zig` - Added cleanup helper \(future-proofing\)

## Test Results

All encoding WPT tests continue to pass:
- Single-byte: 7168/7168 \(100%\)
- Multi-byte: 367/391 \(93.9%\)
- Invalid label: 3421/3421 \(100%\)

title: Fix conversions.zig toV8Value to convert Global handles to Local handles
description:
## Problem

In `src/runtime/engines/v8/conversions.zig` around line ~1546, `toV8Value` returns `h.ptr` \(raw `Global\<Value\>*` pointer\) instead of calling `v8_Global_Get\(\)` to convert it to a `Local\<Value\>`.

## Impact

V8 sees a raw C++ pointer as a JavaScript number, causing "TypeError: number 791666112 is not a function" errors when callbacks are invoked.

## Required Fix

When the value is a Global handle, call `v8_Global_Get\(isolate, h.ptr\)` to obtain a proper `Local\<Value\>` before returning.

## Location

`src/runtime/engines/v8/conversions.zig` line ~1546

Implement the ReadableStreamGenericReader mixin which is currently a stub.

## Problem

src/webidl/impls/ReadableStreamGenericReader.zig

pub fn get_closed(instance: *runtime.Instance) ImplError!*const anyopaque {

pub fn call_cancel(instance: *runtime.Instance, reason: *const anyopaque) ImplError!*const anyopaque {

}

description:

1. **Node.cloneNode(deep)** - Clone a node

   - Required by: Document.importNode(), Range operations
   - Test: Clone all node types, deep vs shallow, attribute preservation
   
2. **Node.normalize()** - Text node normalization

description:
forEach iteration must handle collection modifications correctly.

Parent: whatwg-im39o \(WebIDL WPT 100%\)

Failing tests \(3 in iterator-invalidation-foreach.html\):
- forEach will not iterate over elements removed during iteration
- Removing elements already iterated over during forEach will cause iterator to skip an element
- Elements added during iteration with forEach will be reached

Current behavior shows extra iterations or missing iterations when the collection is modified.

Required behavior:
1. forEach uses a live iterator over the collection
2. Removing an item that hasn't been visited yet: that item is skipped
3. Removing an already-visited item: iteration continues, may skip next item
4. Adding items: newly added items should be visited if they come after current position

This affects URLSearchParams.forEach and similar collection types.

Spec ref: WebIDL §3.7.7 forEach operations

title: [Phase 1.1] Implement header list multimap data structure
description:
## Summary
Implement the internal header list data structure as specified in the Fetch standard.

## Spec Reference
- https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list
- specs/whatwg/fetch.md (Headers section)

## Location
`src/fetch/internal/header_list.zig`

## Requirements

### Data Structure
A header list is a specialized multimap: an ordered list of key-value pairs with potentially duplicate keys.

```zig
pub const HeaderList = struct {
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    entries: std.ArrayList(Header),
    
    pub const Header = struct {
        name: []const u8,  // header name (case-preserved but case-insensitive matching)
        value: []const u8, // header value
    };
};
```

### Required Operations (per spec)

1. **contains(name)** - Check if list contains header name (byte-case-insensitive)
2. **get(name)** - Get combined value of all headers with name, separated by `, `
3. **get_decode_split(name)** - Get, decode (isomorphic), and split on commas
4. **append(name, value)** - Append header, reusing existing name casing
5. **delete(name)** - Remove all headers with name
6. **set(name, value)** - Set first header with name, remove others
7. **combine(name, value)** - Combine with existing value using `, `
8. **sort_and_combine()** - Sort by lowercase name, combine values (special handling for Set-Cookie)
9. **clone()** - Deep copy the header list

### Special Cases
- Set-Cookie headers are NEVER combined (spec requirement)
- Header names must match field-name token production
- Header values must not have leading/trailing HTTP whitespace
- Header values must not contain NUL or HTTP newline bytes

### Normalization
```zig
/// Normalize header value: remove leading/trailing HTTP whitespace
pub fn normalize(value: []const u8) []const u8
```

### Memory Management
- All strings must be owned copies (allocated)
- Proper cleanup in deinit()
- Use errdefer for error paths

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 9 operations implemented per spec
- [ ] Set-Cookie special handling correct
- [ ] Case-insensitive matching for names
- [ ] Case-preserving storage for names
- [ ] Memory leak free (test with testing.allocator)
- [ ] Unit tests for all operations
- [ ] Unit tests for edge cases (empty values, special chars)

## Dependencies
- None (foundational)

## Blocked By
- None

## Blocks

- Phase 2.x (request/response internals)
- Phase 7.x (Headers interface)

title: WPT runner performance: Context reuse instead of recreate per test
description:
## Problem

WPT runner is extremely slow - ~11 seconds per test (4 minutes for 21 tests). This makes running the full WPT suite impractical.

## Investigation Results

**Context reuse IS working:**
- Init testharness: ~4ms (fast!)
- Execute test: ~9,950ms (the bottleneck)

The bottleneck is NOT V8 context creation - it's testharness.js's internal timeout.

**Root Cause:**
1. testharness.js has a 10-second default timeout
2. Each test file has at least 1 subtest that times out (due to missing APIs)
3. The harness waits for the full timeout before signaling completion
4. This means EVERY test file takes ~10 seconds regardless of actual execution time

**Evidence:**
- : 8 subtests, 4 pass, 4 fail, 1 TIMEOUT
- The test file status is TIMEOUT even though all subtests have results
- testharness.js completion callback is called after ~9.8 seconds

## What Was Implemented

1. **Context reuse** - BrowserAdapter maintains single V8 context across tests
2. **JS state reset** - resetJavaScriptState() resets testharness.js state between tests (~4ms)
3. **Console stub** - Added basic console.log/warn/error/info stubs to prevent JS errors
4. **META script loading** - Load external scripts from  comments
5. **Relative URL fetch** - Resolve relative URLs for WPT test resources
6. **Debug callback** - Added __wpt_debug_log for debugging testharness.js

## Resolution

**CLOSING** - Context reuse is fully implemented and working. The remaining performance issue (10s per test) is NOT fixable by V8 optimizations - it requires fixing the test environment.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [x] Context reuse implemented (4ms init time)
- [x] JS state reset between tests
- [ ] ~~WPT url/ tests complete in under 1 minute~~ - Blocked by testharness.js timeout issue

**Next Steps (separate issues needed):**
1. Add missing test environment APIs (structuredClone, document.createElement)
2. Configure shorter testharness.js timeouts for fast tests
3. Investigate why subtests timeout

## Files Modified

-  - Complete rewrite for context reuse
-  - Added resetJavaScriptState, console, debug callback
-  - Added META script loading
-  - Disabled snapshot_generator default install
-  - Fixed stdout API for Zig 0.15

- `tmp/async_iterator_research.md`

1. **`src/streams/internal/algorithm.zig`**

   - Supports native Zig closures with context

4. **`src/streams/internal/from_iterable_algorithm.zig`**

title: Handle document.write\(\) during vs after parsing
description:
## Summary

document.write\(\) behaves differently during parsing \(inserts into stream\) vs after parsing \(implicitly calls document.open\(\)\).

## HTML Spec Reference

HTML Standard §8.4.2:
- **During parsing**: Content inserted at insertion point
- **After parsing** \(insertion_point = null\): 
  - Calls document.open\(\) implicitly
  - Opens a new document, erasing existing content
  - Starts a new parser

## Current State

`DocumentWriteState` already has logic for this:
```zig
if \(state.insertion_point == null\) {
    if \(state.ignore_destructive_writes_counter \> 0 or state.unload_counter \> 0\) {
        return\; // Ignored
    }
    try documentOpen\(state\)\;
}
```

## Implementation

1. **Track parsing state**:
   - Set `insertion_point` when parser starts
   - Clear `insertion_point` when parser finishes
   - Document needs to know if parsing is active

2. **During-parsing behavior**:
   - Insert directly into InputStreamManager
   - Parser sees new content immediately
   - No document.open\(\) call

3. **After-parsing behavior**:
   - Call document.open\(\) \(erases document\)
   - Buffer content
   - Parse when document.close\(\) is called

4. **ignore-destructive-writes counter**:
   - Incremented during external script execution
   - When \> 0, document.write\(\) that would call open\(\) is ignored
   - Already in spec, need to increment/decrement properly

## Files to Modify

- `src/html/document_write.zig` \(already has most logic\)
- `src/webidl/impls/Document.zig` \(expose state\)
- `src/html/script_execution.zig` \(set counters\)

## Test Criteria

```html
\<\!-- During parsing --\>
\<script\>
  document.write\('\<p\>inserted\</p\>'\)\;
\</script\>
\<\!-- p element appears inline --\>

\<\!-- After parsing --\>
\<script\>
  setTimeout\(\(\) =\> {
    document.write\('\<p\>replaced\</p\>'\)\;
    // Entire document replaced
  }, 0\)\;
\</script\>
```

description:
## Revised Scope After Spec Analysis

Original task requested migrating promise callbacks to TypedCallback. After analyzing WHATWG Streams spec and WebIDL spec, the actual issues are:

1. **AsyncPromise.onSettleCtx has a critical bug** \(unsafe void-to-T cast\) → See whatwg-uobjb
2. **Some values use anyopaque instead of spec-mandated `any` type** → Use runtime.JSValue
3. **Algorithm creation is inconsistent** → Standardize on createTypedAlgorithm

### What Does NOT Need Changing:
- VTable pattern in Algorithm is correct \(spec doesn't specify implementation\)
- AsyncPromise reaction context using anyopaque is correct for polymorphism
- The `@ptrCast\(@alignCast\(ctx\)\)` patterns in VTable functions are unavoidable with type erasure

### New Sub-Tasks Created:
- whatwg-uobjb \(P0\): Fix AsyncPromise.onSettleCtx unsafe cast
- whatwg-3hjs1 \(P1\): Replace AbortRequest.reason with runtime.JSValue
- whatwg-incgy \(P2\): Standardize Algorithm creation

### Spec References:
- Streams spec uses `any` type for: cancel reasons, abort reasons, chunks, error values
- Controllers are strongly typed \(ReadableStreamDefaultController, etc.\)
- WebIDL `any` should map to `runtime.JSValue` tagged union, NOT `*anyopaque`

This task can be closed once the sub-tasks are complete.

comments.author: bcardarella
comments.text:
Analysis complete:
- 4 promise callback functions with `fn \(*anyopaque, void\) anyerror\!void` signatures
- 26+ `@ptrCast\(@alignCast\(...\)\)` patterns
- Main callbacks: onStartFulfilledCallback, onByteStartFulfilledCallback, onStartFulfilled, onByteStartFulfilled
- This is a significant refactoring requiring careful implementation to avoid breaking stream operations

comments.author: bcardarella
comments.text:
## Analysis: This task should be reconsidered

After reviewing the code, the `*anyopaque` usage in ReadableStream.zig callbacks falls into **legitimate VTable/polymorphism patterns** that are explicitly allowed per AGENTS.md Golden Rule #10.

### Why these patterns are intentional:

1. **AsyncPromise.onSettleCtx API** - The promise callback infrastructure \(`src/streams/internal/async_promise.zig`\) fundamentally uses `*anyopaque` context in its `Reaction` struct \(line 155\). This is by design to allow any type to be passed as callback context.

2. **Algorithm VTable pattern** - The `Algorithm` type uses VTable polymorphism with `context: ?*anyopaque` - this matches the standard Zig VTable pattern \(like `std.mem.Allocator`\).

3. **Callback signatures match promise API** - The callbacks like `onStartFulfilledCallback\(ctx: *anyopaque, ...\)` are designed to match the signature expected by `AsyncPromise.onSettleCtx`.

### The TypedCallback module is for different use cases:
- Timer callbacks \(external API\)
- GC finalizers \(external API\)
- Work callbacks \(thread pool\)

It was NOT designed to replace internal promise reaction handling.

### Options:
1. **Close as "won't fix"** - The current pattern is correct and idiomatic
2. **Convert to architecture task** - Redesign AsyncPromise to use generics \(large scope change\)
3. **Narrow scope** - Only target the 3-4 V8-specific `callconv\(.c\)` callbacks which could use `SelfContainedPromiseCallback`

Recommend option 1 or 3.

comments.author: bcardarella
comments.text:
## Revised Analysis After Spec Review

Based on thorough analysis of WHATWG Streams spec and current implementation:

### Key Findings:

1. **The spec uses `any` type, NOT untyped pointers** - Cancel reasons, abort reasons, chunks, and error values should use `runtime.JSValue` \(a tagged union representing JS values\), NOT `*anyopaque`.

2. **Critical Bug Found in AsyncPromise.onSettleCtx** - Lines 426-427 unsafely cast `void`-returning functions to `T`-returning functions. This is undefined behavior.

3. **VTable pattern is correct but context should be typed** - The Algorithm VTable pattern is sound, but we should use `createTypedAlgorithm` consistently.

### Spec-Aligned Refactoring Plan:

**Phase 1: Fix AsyncPromise.onSettleCtx bug \(Critical\)**
- Create separate `FireAndForgetReaction` type for void-returning handlers
- Don't cast void to T

**Phase 2: Replace `?*const anyopaque` reason/error with `runtime.JSValue`**
- `TeeState.reason1/reason2` → `runtime.JSValue` ✅ \(already done in whatwg-0qz0h\)
- `AbortRequest.reason` → `runtime.JSValue`
- `PipeState` error reasons → `runtime.JSValue`
- All `error\(e: *const anyopaque\)` → `error\(e: runtime.JSValue\)`

**Phase 3: Use TypedAlgorithm consistently**
- Replace manual Algorithm creation with `createTypedAlgorithm` factory
- Eliminates ad-hoc anyopaque usage in algorithm contexts

### Verdict:
This task should be **restructured** into specific, spec-aligned sub-tasks rather than attempting to migrate to TypedCallback \(which was designed for a different purpose\).

title: Add defensive alignment validation in v8_wrapper.cpp
description:
## Summary

Add defensive alignment checks in the C++ V8 wrapper layer to catch misaligned pointers before they cause cryptic crashes.

## Location

**File:** `src/runtime/engines/v8/v8_wrapper.cpp`

## Changes Required

### 1. Add Alignment Check Macro

```cpp
// At top of file
#define CHECK_ALIGNED\(ptr, type\) \
    do { \
        if \(\(reinterpret_cast\<uintptr_t\>\(ptr\) \& \(alignof\(type\) - 1\)\) \!= 0\) { \
            fprintf\(stderr, "ERROR: Misaligned pointer %p for type %s \(requires %zu alignment\)\n", \
                    static_cast\<const void*\>\(ptr\), #type, alignof\(type\)\)\; \
            return nullptr\; \
        } \
    } while \(0\)
```

### 2. Add Checks to Key Functions

**v8_Object_Get \(line ~1080\):**
```cpp
Global\<Value\>* v8_Object_Get\(Global\<Object\>* object, Global\<Context\>* context, Global\<Value\>* key\) {
    CHECK_ALIGNED\(object, Global\<Object\>\)\;
    CHECK_ALIGNED\(context, Global\<Context\>\)\;
    CHECK_ALIGNED\(key, Global\<Value\>\)\;
    
    Isolate* isolate = Isolate::GetCurrent\(\)\;
    // ... rest of function
}
```

**v8_Object_Set:**
```cpp
bool v8_Object_Set\(Global\<Object\>* object, Global\<Context\>* context, Global\<Value\>* key, Global\<Value\>* value\) {
    CHECK_ALIGNED\(object, Global\<Object\>\)\;
    CHECK_ALIGNED\(context, Global\<Context\>\)\;
    CHECK_ALIGNED\(key, Global\<Value\>\)\;
    CHECK_ALIGNED\(value, Global\<Value\>\)\;
    // ...
}
```

### 3. Functions to Instrument

Add alignment checks to all functions that receive `Global\<T\>*` pointers:

- `v8_Object_Get`
- `v8_Object_Set`
- `v8_Object_Has`
- `v8_Object_Delete`
- `v8_Object_GetPropertyNames`
- `v8_Object_InternalFieldCount`
- `v8_Object_GetAlignedPointerFromInternalField`
- `v8_Object_SetAlignedPointerInInternalField`
- `v8_Function_Call`
- `v8_Function_NewInstance`
- `v8_Value_*` functions
- Any other function receiving pointer parameters

### 4. Optional: Debug Build Only

For production builds, make checks conditional:

```cpp
#ifdef DEBUG
#define CHECK_ALIGNED\(ptr, type\) /* ... full check ... */
#else
#define CHECK_ALIGNED\(ptr, type\) \(\(void\)0\)
#endif
```

## Benefits

1. **Clear error messages** instead of cryptic "upcast of misaligned address"
2. **Earlier detection** - catch at FFI boundary, not deep in V8
3. **Function name in error** - easier to trace call site
4. **Optional overhead** - can disable in release builds

## Testing

1. Build with checks enabled
2. Run WPT without fixes - should see clear error messages
3. Apply fixes - should run without errors

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `CHECK_ALIGNED` macro added
- [ ] All pointer-receiving functions instrumented
- [ ] Error messages include function name and pointer value
- [ ] Conditional compilation for debug/release

11 weeks total across 6 phases

Remove all `@ptrFromInt\(1\)` sentinel value usages that represent "undefined" and replace with proper `JSValue.undefined` or null.

## Problem

The codebase uses `@ptrFromInt\(1\)` as a sentinel value for "undefined":

```zig
// Current dangerous pattern
const error_ptr: *const anyopaque = if \(e.was_passed\) e.value else @ptrFromInt\(1\)\;
```

This is dangerous because:
1. `1` is not a valid pointer - will crash if dereferenced
2. Receivers must know to check for this magic value
3. Easy to forget the check and crash
4. Not self-documenting

## Files with @ptrFromInt\(1\) Usage

From the audit \(~30+ usages\):

\| File \| Count \| Context \|
\|------\|-------\|---------\|
\| Element.zig \| 17 \| ARIA element references \|
\| ReadableStreamDefaultController.zig \| 2 \| Error/chunk passthrough \|
\| ReadableStreamBYOBReader.zig \| 1 \| View handling \|
\| TextEncoderStream.zig \| 1 \| Chunk handling \|
\| MessageEvent.zig \| 3 \| Event data \|
\| NavigationDestination.zig \| 1 \| State \|
\| Selection.zig \| 1 \| Range \|
\| Text.zig \| 1 \| Split \|
\| CountQueuingStrategy.zig \| 1 \| Size function \|
\| ReadableStream.zig \| 1 \| Reason \|
\| NavigationHistoryEntry.zig \| 1 \| State \|

## Search Command

```bash
rg "@ptrFromInt\\(1\\)" src/webidl/impls/ --type zig
```

## Replacement Strategy

### For files already migrated to JSValue:

```zig
// BEFORE
const error_ptr: *const anyopaque = if \(e.was_passed\) e.value else @ptrFromInt\(1\)\;

// AFTER
const error_value: JSValue = if \(e.wasPassed\(\)\) e.getValue\(\) else .{ .undefined = {} }\;
```

### For files not yet migrated \(use null\):

```zig
// BEFORE
const error_ptr: *const anyopaque = if \(e.was_passed\) e.value else @ptrFromInt\(1\)\;

// AFTER
const error_ptr: ?*const anyopaque = if \(e.was_passed\) e.value else null\;
```

### Update consumers to check properly:

```zig
// BEFORE \(checking for sentinel\)
if \(@intFromPtr\(ptr\) == 1\) { ... }

// AFTER \(null check\)
if \(ptr == null\) { ... }
// OR with JSValue
if \(value.isUndefined\(\)\) { ... }
```

## Implementation Steps

1. Search for all @ptrFromInt\(1\) usages
2. For each usage:
   a. Determine if the file should use JSValue \(if already converted\) or null
   b. Update the assignment
   c. Update all consumers of that value
3. Search for @intFromPtr comparisons with 1
4. Update those checks
5. Run tests to verify

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Zero `@ptrFromInt\(1\)` in codebase \(except legitimate use cases like null ptr patterns\)
- [ ] All former sentinel usages use either `JSValue.undefined` or `null`
- [ ] All consumers updated to use proper checks
- [ ] No crashes from dereferencing sentinel values
- [ ] All tests pass

title: WPT tests take 10 seconds each due to completion callback not firing
description:
## Problem
WPT tests take 10 seconds each (the timeout duration) because the completion callback never sets .

## Root Cause Investigation

1. **Timer system works correctly**:
   -  schedules timer
   - libuv timer fires
   -  calls the JavaScript function
   - The function returns successfully

2. **JavaScript callback chain is broken**:
   - Our completion script calls  (testharness.js exposed function)
   -  is supposed to trigger  handlers
   - Our  registers  to call 
   - But  is never called

3. **Suspected cause**:
   -  is undefined after testharness.js reload
   - When testharness.js is reloaded, it creates a new environment
   - The callbacks registered in  are cleared
   - Even though we re-register them,  is never set to true

## Debug Evidence


## Potential Fixes
1. Don't reload testharness.js - instead properly reset its internal state
2. Create a fresh V8 context for each test (slower but more reliable)
3. Use V8 snapshots to make fresh context creation fast
4. Find a way to properly initialize  after reload

## Workaround
Reduce timeout to 1 second to speed up test runs at the cost of potentially missing slow tests.

title: WebIDL codegen inconsistently snake_cases interface file names
description:
The WebIDL codegen preserves source file names when generating output, but source files have inconsistent naming conventions:

**Problem:**
- Some sources: Element.zig, Attr.zig, Node.zig (PascalCase)
- Generated outputs: element.zig, attr.zig, node.zig (snake_case)
- Other sources: AbortController.zig (PascalCase)
- Generated outputs: AbortController.zig (PascalCase preserved)

**Root Cause:**
The codegen does NOT snake_case files - it preserves source names. The inconsistency exists in webidl/src/ which is not in git. Some files were created with snake_case names, others with PascalCase.

**Impact:**
- Confusing naming conventions
- Mixed import styles
- Hard to predict generated file names

**Solution:**
1. Standardize all source files in webidl/src/ to PascalCase
2. Update codegen to enforce naming convention
3. OR: Add explicit file naming transform in codegen

**Affected Files:**
- webidl/src/dom/Attr.zig → webidl/generated/dom/attr.zig
- webidl/src/dom/Element.zig → webidl/generated/dom/element.zig
- webidl/src/dom/Node.zig → webidl/generated/dom/node.zig
- webidl/src/dom/Event.zig → webidl/generated/dom/event.zig
- webidl/src/dom/Comment.zig → webidl/generated/dom/comment.zig
- webidl/src/dom/Document.zig → webidl/generated/dom/document.zig
- webidl/src/dom/Text.zig → webidl/generated/dom/text.zig

vs consistently PascalCase:
- AbortController.zig, EventTarget.zig, NodeList.zig, etc.

**Related Investigation:**
- Codegen uses pascalToSnakeCase() only for module imports, NOT file naming
- File names are preserved from source
- Source directory (webidl/src/) not tracked in git
notes: Cannot complete rename on case-insensitive macOS filesystem. Two-step git mv creates duplicate file references. Need to either: (1) perform rename on Linux/case-sensitive FS, or (2) manually create new PascalCase files and delete old ones. Source files in webidl/src/dom/ need rename: attr.zig→Attr.zig, comment.zig→Comment.zig, document.zig→Document.zig, element.zig→Element.zig, event.zig→Event.zig, node.zig→Node.zig, text.zig→Text.zig

title: [SW Phase 3] Client-Side WebIDL Interfaces
[SW Phase 4] ServiceWorkerGlobalScope and Context APIs
[SW Phase 5] Service Worker Events
[SW Phase 6] Cache API
[SW Phase 7] Core Algorithms
description:
Implement core Service Worker algorithms from Appendix A.

## Background

These algorithms define the SW lifecycle and behavior. They're the heart of the specification.

## Tasks

### 7.1 Job Processing
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/jobs.zig`

Algorithms:
- **Create Job**: Initialize job with parameters
- **Schedule Job**: Add job to queue, deduplicate equivalent jobs
- **Run Job**: Execute job based on type
- **Finish Job**: Resolve promises, process equivalent jobs

### 7.2 Register Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/register.zig`

Steps (per spec Appendix A):
1. Validate scriptURL (same-origin, secure context)
2. Resolve scope URL
3. Get or create registration
4. If registration exists with same scriptURL, resolve immediately
5. Otherwise, schedule Update job

### 7.3 Update Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/update.zig`

Steps:
1. Get registration's newest worker
2. Fetch script (byte-for-byte check against existing)
3. If script unchanged and not forced, abort
4. Create new ServiceWorker in 'parsed' state
5. Update registration's installing worker
6. Fire 'updatefound' event
7. Run Install algorithm

### 7.4 Install Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/install.zig`

Steps:
1. Set worker state to 'installing'
2. Fire 'install' event on global scope
3. Wait for ExtendableEvent to complete
4. If event has errors, fail installation
5. Set worker state to 'installed'
6. If no active worker, run Activate
7. Otherwise, wait for activation conditions

### 7.5 Activate Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/activate.zig`

Steps:
1. Set worker state to 'activating'
2. Move worker from waiting to active
3. Fire 'activate' event
4. Wait for ExtendableEvent to complete
5. Set worker state to 'activated'
6. Update controlled clients

### 7.6 Run Service Worker Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/run_worker.zig`

Steps:
1. Create ServiceWorkerGlobalScope
2. Attach to registration
3. Evaluate worker script (via mock)
4. Start handling events
5. Return completion status

### 7.7 Terminate Service Worker Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/terminate.zig`

Steps:
1. Clear event handlers
2. Abort all pending fetch operations
3. Clear timers
4. Detach from global scope
5. Run termination cleanup

### 7.8 Handle Fetch Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/handle_fetch.zig`

This is the core algorithm for request interception:

Steps:
1. Let registration be the controlling registration
2. If no active worker, return null (no interception)
3. Check router rules first (if any)
4. If router says 'network', skip SW
5. If router says 'cache', check cache
6. If router says 'fetch-event', dispatch to SW
7. Create FetchEvent with request
8. Set preloadResponse if navigation preload enabled
9. Dispatch event to worker
10. If respondWith() called, use that response
11. Otherwise, fallback to network fetch

### 7.9 Soft Update Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/soft_update.zig`

Schedule update without user interaction:
- Check last update time
- If stale (24+ hours), schedule update job
- Don't force bypass cache

### 7.10 Try Clear Registration Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/clear_registration.zig`

Check if registration can be removed:
- No installing, waiting, or active worker
- No controlled clients
- Remove from registration map

### 7.11 Try Activate Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/try_activate.zig`

Check activation conditions:
- Has waiting worker
- No active worker OR active worker has no controlled clients
- skipWaiting was called

### 7.12 Get Newest Worker Algorithm
Location: `src/service_worker/algorithms/get_newest.zig`

Return worker in order: installing > waiting > active

## Spec References

- All algorithms: specs/w3c/service-workers.md Appendix A

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All algorithms implemented per spec
- [ ] Job queue properly orders operations
- [ ] Lifecycle transitions correct (parsed -> installing -> installed -> activating -> activated -> redundant)
- [ ] Handle Fetch correctly intercepts requests
- [ ] Router rules evaluated correctly
- [ ] Navigation preload works
- [ ] All edge cases handled (errors, timeouts)
- [ ] Integration tests for full lifecycle

title: [SW Phase 8] Fetch Integration
description:
Wire Service Worker interception into the existing Fetch implementation.

## Background

The Fetch spec defines hooks for Service Worker interception. Our fetch implementation has TODO comments for this. This phase connects them.

## Tasks

### 8.1 Update HTTP Fetch Algorithm
Location: `src/fetch/algorithms/http_fetch.zig`

The existing TODO in http_fetch.zig:
```zig
// TODO: Service Worker interception
// 1. If request's service-workers mode is "all", handle SW
// 2. Call Handle Fetch algorithm
// 3. If response from SW, use it
// 4. Otherwise continue with network fetch
```

Implementation:
1. Check if request's service-workers mode is "all"
2. Get the active service worker registration for the request's client
3. Call Handle Fetch algorithm from Phase 7
4. If response returned, use it
5. Otherwise proceed with normal fetch

### 8.2 Add Service Worker Mode to Request
Location: `src/fetch/request.zig`

Ensure Request has:
```zig
pub const ServiceWorkersMode = enum {
    all,    // Allow SW interception
    none,   // Bypass SW
};

pub const Request = struct {
    // ... existing fields ...
    service_workers_mode: ServiceWorkersMode = .all,
};
```

### 8.3 Navigation Preload Integration
Location: `src/fetch/algorithms/http_fetch.zig`

For navigation requests with preload enabled:
1. Start network fetch in parallel with SW dispatch
2. Make preload response available via FetchEvent.preloadResponse
3. If SW uses preloadResponse, avoid duplicate fetch

### 8.4 Response Source Tracking
Location: `src/fetch/response.zig`

Add tracking for response source:
```zig
pub const ResponseSource = enum {
    network,
    cache,
    service_worker,
    service_worker_cache,
    navigation_preload,
};
```

### 8.5 Timing Integration
Location: `src/fetch/timing.zig`

Add Service Worker timing fields:
- `workerStart`: when SW started for this fetch
- `workerRouterEvaluationStart`: router rule evaluation start
- `workerCacheLookupStart`: cache lookup start (if routed to cache)
- `finalResponseHeadersReceived`: when response headers available

### 8.6 Handle Controlled Clients
Location: `src/service_worker/integration/controlled_fetch.zig`

Helper to determine if a client is controlled:
1. Get client's environment settings object
2. Look up active service worker
3. Check scope matches request URL

### 8.7 Error Handling

Handle SW interception failures:
- SW throws error -> return network error response
- SW times out -> fallback to network
- respondWith promise rejects -> network error
- Invalid response from SW -> network error

### 8.8 Request Cloning for SW

Service Workers receive a clone of the request:
- Clone request before passing to SW
- Original request can still be used for network fetch
- Handle body stream cloning correctly

## Spec References

- Fetch Standard § 4.6 HTTP fetch: https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-fetch
- Service Workers § Handle Fetch: specs/w3c/service-workers.md Appendix A

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fetch correctly checks for SW interception
- [ ] Handle Fetch algorithm is called at right point
- [ ] SW responses are used correctly
- [ ] Fallback to network works when SW doesn't respond
- [ ] Navigation preload works
- [ ] Timing info correctly populated
- [ ] Error cases handled gracefully
- [ ] service-workers mode "none" bypasses SW
- [ ] Integration tests with mock SW responses

title: Implement String Interning for Tag Names
description:
**Location:** `Element.zig`, `HTMLParser.zig`

**Problem:** Same tag names \(div, span, p, etc.\) are allocated repeatedly throughout document parsing.

**Solution:** Maintain intern pool for common strings. Return pointer to existing interned string instead of allocating new copy.

**Expected Impact:** 15-25% reduction in string allocations. Also enables O\(1\) tag name comparison via pointer equality.

title: Epic: Make Codegen Authoritative - Move All Interface Customizations to Impls
description:
## Problem

Running codegen currently overwrites 1237 files, removing manual customizations. This makes codegen unusable for keeping interfaces in sync with IDL changes.

## Current State After Investigation

**VTable Deinit**: ✅ Already implemented in codegen (writer.zig line 1693). Committed interface files have stale code from before this feature was added.

**Typedef Naming**: Can be improved but is blocked by deeper issue - callers expect hand-written typedefs with richer types (HeadersInit has pairs/record/headers_ptr, BodyInit has string/blob/etc).

**Interface Custom Functions**: These exist in interfaces and delegate to impls. Codegen removes them. The functions ARE in impls, but callers import interfaces.

## Blockers Discovered

1. **Typedef type mismatch**: Generated typedefs use  for all union variants. Hand-written typedefs have rich types like  for pairs. Callers expect the rich types.

2. **Dictionary field names**: Generated dictionaries may have different field names than callers expect (e.g., RequestInit.method).

3. **IterableEntry missing**: FormData.zig impl expects FormData.IterableEntry which codegen doesn't generate.

4. **Root exports**: typedefs/root.zig doesn't export types from manual typedefs (HeaderEntry).

## Revised Scope

This is a much larger effort than initially estimated. Options:

**Option A: Update codegen to match current code**
- Generate richer typedef types
- Generate IterableEntry types
- Preserve dictionary field names
- Add custom function stubs in interfaces
- Estimated: 2-3 weeks

**Option B: Update all callers to match generated code**
- Change ~20+ impl files to use new typedef field names
- Change script_execution.zig to use impls
- Change interface.zig stream callbacks to use impls
- Update conversions.zig for simpler types
- Estimated: 1-2 weeks

**Option C: Hybrid approach**
- Mark certain files as "manual" and skip in codegen
- Only regenerate files that don't have custom code
- Gradually migrate custom code to proper locations
- Estimated: 1 week initial, ongoing maintenance

## Current Progress

- [x] VTable deinit pattern - already in codegen (issue can be closed)
- [ ] Typedef union naming - blocked on type richness issue
- [ ] Move Document custom functions - blocked on caller updates
- [ ] Move HTMLScriptElement custom functions - blocked on caller updates  
- [ ] Move stream callbacks - blocked on caller updates
- [ ] Move remaining custom functions - blocked on caller updates
- [ ] Update callers - large scope, needs dedicated effort

## Recommendation

Start with Option C (hybrid approach) to unblock codegen usage:
1. Add manual typedef skip list
2. Add manual interface skip list (for files with custom functions)
3. Document which files are manual vs generated
4. Create follow-up epics for full migration

## Summary
`src/streams/internal/algorithms/reader_ops.zig` line 237 uses `@alignCast\(@constCast` on cancel promise.

const cancel_promise: *AsyncPromise\(void\) = @ptrCast\(@alignCast\(@constCast\(cancel_promise_ptr\)\)\)\;

Use `pointer_tag.untagPointer\(\)` before casting.

title: Fix reader_ops.zig anyopaque callback parameters
description:
## Summary

reader_ops.zig uses `*anyopaque` for callback context and chunk values in readableStreamDefaultReaderRead.

## Current Code \(reader_ops.zig:70-76\)

```zig
pub fn readableStreamDefaultReaderRead\(
    reader: *runtime.Instance,
    context: *anyopaque,
    chunk_steps: *const fn \(ctx: *anyopaque, chunk: *anyopaque\) void,
    close_steps: *const fn \(ctx: *anyopaque\) void,
    error_steps: *const fn \(ctx: *anyopaque\) void,
\) \!void {
```

## Solution

Use typed callbacks or a callback interface:

```zig
pub const ReadCallbacks = struct {
    context: *anyopaque,
    chunk_steps: *const fn \(ctx: *anyopaque, chunk: runtime.JSValue\) void,
    close_steps: *const fn \(ctx: *anyopaque\) void,
    error_steps: *const fn \(ctx: *anyopaque, err: webidl.errors.Exception\) void,
}\;

pub fn readableStreamDefaultReaderRead\(
    reader: *runtime.Instance,
    callbacks: ReadCallbacks,
\) \!void {
```

Or use generics:

```zig
pub fn readableStreamDefaultReaderRead\(
    comptime Context: type,
    reader: *runtime.Instance,
    context: *Context,
    comptime callbacks: ReadCallbackFns\(Context\),
\) \!void {
```

## Files to Modify

- `src/streams/internal/algorithms/reader_ops.zig`
- `src/streams/internal/readable_stream_async_iterator.zig` \(caller\)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Context is type-safe or properly documented
- [ ] Chunk values use runtime.JSValue not anyopaque
- [ ] Error values use proper Exception type
- [ ] Tests pass

title: Phase 4, Week 8: Upload Progress & CORS Integration
description:
## Overview

Complete upload progress tracking and verify CORS integration with Fetch API.

## Objectives

1. **Upload Progress**: Track upload body transmission, fire progress events on XMLHttpRequestUpload object
2. **CORS Integration**: Verify XHR correctly uses Fetch CORS mode, test withCredentials flag
3. **Upload Event Ordering**: Ensure upload events fire before download events

## Upload Progress Details

- Upload object has same events as XHR (loadstart, progress, load, etc.)
- Progress events throttled to 50ms (separate tracker from download)
- Upload events fire during request transmission
- Upload complete before response begins

## CORS Integration

- XHR always uses CORS mode (req.mode = .cors)
- withCredentials controls credentials mode (.include vs .same_origin)
- Upload listeners trigger CORS preflight (spec requirement!)
- CORS headers handled by Fetch (reuse existing)

## Spec References

- Upload: https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-xmlhttprequestupload
- CORS: https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-cors-protocol

## Acceptance Criteria

- Upload progress events fire correctly
- Upload events fire before download events
- 50ms throttling works for upload
- withCredentials controls CORS credentials
- Upload listeners trigger preflight
- Tests verify event ordering

## Estimated Effort

1 week

# 7.3: Wire postMessage to structured clone and MessageEvent

## Objective
Connect postMessage to structured clone algorithm and dispatch MessageEvents.

## Current State
- Structured clone fully implemented in src/html/structured_clone/
- MessagePort interface exists
- Worker postMessage is defined but doesn't work
- outside_port/inside_port are null

## Implementation

1. Create MessagePort pair on worker creation
2. Entangle ports (main thread port <-> worker port)
3. postMessage: serialize with structuredClone, queue to other port
4. Port receives: deserialize, create MessageEvent, dispatch

## Message Flow
Main thread: worker.postMessage(data) 
  -> structuredSerializeWithTransfer(data)
  -> queue to worker's inside_port
Worker: receives from inside_port
  -> structuredDeserializeWithTransfer(data)
  -> create MessageEvent
  -> dispatch to WorkerGlobalScope

**Context**: Simplified Chinese GB18030 encoding direct UTF-8 output.

**Files**:
- `src/encoding/chinese/gb18030.zig`
- `src/encoding/chinese/gb18030_streaming.zig`
- `src/encoding/chinese/gb18030_ranges.zig`

**GB18030 Structure**:
- ASCII \(0x00-0x7F\): pass through
- 2-byte sequences: lead \(0x81-0xFE\) + trail
- 4-byte sequences: for code points outside BMP \(uses ranges\)

**Complexity**: Higher due to range-based 4-byte decoding.

**Implementation**:
1. Detect sequence length
2. For 2-byte: use index lookup
3. For 4-byte: use range calculation
4. Emit UTF-8 directly \(including 4-byte UTF-8 for supplementary chars\)

- [ ] `decodeToUtf8` implemented for GB18030
- [ ] 4-byte sequences decode correctly to supplementary characters

description:
## Overview

Create the bridge layer that allows V8 to use our Zig i18n library instead of ICU.

## V8 Integration Approaches

### Option 1: V8 Extension \(Recommended\)
Replace V8's built-in Intl with JavaScript wrappers that call Zig via FFI.

```cpp
// v8_intl_extension.cpp
void DateTimeFormat_Format\(const FunctionCallbackInfo\<Value\>\& args\) {
    // Extract arguments
    // Call Zig function via C ABI
    // Return result to JS
}
```

### Option 2: Patch V8's Intl
Modify V8's Intl implementation to call Zig instead of ICU. More complex, harder to maintain.

### Option 3: JavaScript Polyfill
Pure JS Intl implementation that calls native functions. Simpler but slower.

## C-Compatible API

```zig
// src/intl/v8_bridge/c_api.zig
pub export fn intl_datetime_format_create\(
    locale: [*:0]const u8,
    options_json: [*:0]const u8
\) ?*DateTimeFormat {
    // Create DateTimeFormat instance
}

pub export fn intl_datetime_format_format\(
    dtf: *DateTimeFormat,
    timestamp_ms: i64,
    out_buffer: [*]u8,
    buffer_len: usize
\) i32 {
    // Format date, return length or error
}

pub export fn intl_datetime_format_destroy\(dtf: *DateTimeFormat\) void {
    dtf.deinit\(\)\;
}
```

## Memory Management

Critical: V8 manages JS object lifecycle, Zig manages i18n object lifecycle.

```cpp
// C++ weak callback to clean up Zig resources
void CleanupCallback\(const WeakCallbackInfo\<DateTimeFormat\>\& data\) {
    intl_datetime_format_destroy\(data.GetParameter\(\)\)\;
}
```

## Build Integration

1. Compile Zig library as static/dynamic library
2. Link with V8 wrapper
3. Register extension at V8 initialization

## Components

1. `src/intl/v8_bridge/c_api.zig` - C-compatible exports
2. `src/runtime/engines/v8/intl_extension.cpp` - V8 extension
3. `src/runtime/engines/v8/intl_binding.zig` - Zig-side binding helpers
4. Build system integration

## Test Strategy

1. Unit tests for C API
2. Integration tests with V8
3. WPT Intl tests through full stack

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] C API designed and exported
- [ ] V8 extension registered at startup
- [ ] DateTimeFormat works through V8
- [ ] Memory properly managed \(no leaks\)
- [ ] Error handling works across boundary
- [ ] Performance acceptable \(\< 10% overhead vs ICU\)

## Complexity

Very High - FFI, V8 internals, memory management across languages.

Implement URLPattern regex generator
description:
Implement generation of regex strings from part lists.

## Location
`src/urlpattern/regex_generator.zig`

## Algorithm: generate regular expression and name list

Per spec, converts a part list into:
1. A regex string for PCRE2
2. A list of group names for extraction

## Regex Generation Rules

For each part:

**fixed_text**: Escape regex metacharacters
```
"foo.bar" → "foo\\.bar"
```

**segment_wildcard**: Match non-separator chars
```
// With default segment wildcard regexp "[^/]+"
":name" → "\(?P\<name\>[^/]+\)"
```

**full_wildcard**: Match anything
```
"*" → "\(?P\<0\>.*\)"
```

**regexp**: Use provided pattern
```
":id\(\\d+\)" → "\(?P\<id\>\\d+\)"
```

## Modifier Handling

```
none:      "pattern"
optional:  "\(?:pattern\)?"
zero_plus: "\(?:pattern\)*"
one_plus:  "\(?:pattern\)+"
```

## Prefix/Suffix Wrapping

Parts with prefix/suffix:
```
prefix + "\(" + modifier_wrapped_pattern + "\)" + suffix
```

## Implementation

```zig
pub fn generateRegexAndNameList\(
    allocator: Allocator,
    parts: []const Part,
    options: Options,
\) \!struct { regex: []const u8, names: []const []const u8 } {
    var result = std.ArrayList\(u8\).init\(allocator\)\;
    var names = std.ArrayList\([]const u8\).init\(allocator\)\;
    
    try result.appendSlice\("^"\)\;
    
    for \(parts\) \|part\| {
        switch \(part.type\) {
            .fixed_text =\> try appendEscaped\(\&result, part.value\),
            .segment_wildcard =\> {
                try names.append\(part.name\)\;
                try result.writer\(\).print\("\(?P\<{s}\>{s}\)", .{
                    part.name, options.segment_wildcard_regexp
                }\)\;
            },
            // ... other cases
        }
    }
    
    try result.appendSlice\("$"\)\;
    return .{ .regex = result.toOwnedSlice\(\), .names = names.toOwnedSlice\(\) }\;
}
```

## Spec Reference
URLPattern spec "generate a regular expression and name list"

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixed text properly escaped
- [ ] Named groups use PCRE2 syntax \(?P\<name\>...\)
- [ ] Modifiers wrap correctly
- [ ] Anchors \(^$\) added
- [ ] Name list matches group order

comments.author: bcardarella
comments.text:
Analysis update:
- Window.zig has 1 placeholder callback pattern \(line 3002\) in requestIdleCallback, not a real timer system
- Worker.zig has 2 callback patterns: processQueuedMessagesCallback \(line 462\) and handleMessageFromWorkerCallback \(line 484\)
- Scope is smaller than originally estimated

comments.author: bcardarella
comments.text:
## Investigation Complete

After examining both Window.zig and Worker.zig, I found that migration to TypedCallback is not straightforward:

### Window.zig \(line 3002\)
The callback is a **placeholder stub** that does nothing:
```zig
fn wrapper\(ctx: ?*anyopaque, deadline: *event_loop.IdleDeadline\) void {
    _ = ctx\;
    _ = deadline\;
    // In full implementation: invoke the JS callback via V8
}
```
Migrating a non-functional placeholder provides no benefit.

### Worker.zig \(line 462\)
The `processQueuedMessagesCallback` is used with the timer API:
```zig
timer.setTimeout\(0, processQueuedMessagesCallback, instance\)\;
```

The timer API \(`src/runtime/timer.zig`\) is designed with `?*anyopaque` user_data:
```zig
pub fn setTimeout\(self: Self, ms: u64, callback: TimerCallback, user_data: ?*anyopaque\) TimerId
```

To use `TypedTimerCallback`, we would need to:
1. Change the timer API to accept typed callbacks \(breaking change\)
2. Or add a parallel typed callback API to the timer system

### Recommendation
Close as "won't fix for now" because:
1. Window callback is a stub
2. Worker callback requires timer API changes
3. The cost/benefit of changing the timer API for this one use case is not favorable

A better approach would be to add typed callback support to the timer API as a separate enhancement when more use cases justify it.

CRITICAL: Fix AsyncPromise.onSettleCtx unsafe void-to-T cast
description:
## Critical Bug

In `src/streams/internal/async_promise.zig` lines 426-427, there's an **unsafe cast** that is undefined behavior:

```zig
.on_fulfilled_ctx = if \(on_fulfilled\) \|f\| @ptrCast\(f\) else null,
.on_rejected_ctx = if \(on_rejected\) \|r\| @ptrCast\(r\) else null,
```

This casts `fn\(*anyopaque, T\) anyerror\!void` to `fn\(*anyopaque, T\) anyerror\!T`. When `T \!= void`, this is **undefined behavior** because:
1. The caller provides a void-returning function
2. The `executeReaction` code tries to use the "return value"
3. This reads garbage from the stack

## Risk

- **Segfaults** when promise reactions complete
- **Memory corruption** from reading garbage "return values"
- **Undefined behavior** per Zig semantics

## Solution

Create a separate reaction type for fire-and-forget handlers:

```zig
/// Reaction without chained promise \(fire-and-forget\)
pub const FireAndForgetReaction = struct {
    on_fulfilled_ctx: ?*const fn \(*anyopaque, T\) anyerror\!void = null,
    on_rejected_ctx: ?*const fn \(*anyopaque, webidl.errors.Exception\) anyerror\!void = null,
    context: ?*anyopaque = null,
}\;

// Store separately from chained reactions
fire_and_forget_reactions: infra.List\(FireAndForgetReaction\),
```

Then `onSettleCtx` appends to `fire_and_forget_reactions` instead of using unsafe casts.

## Files to Modify

- `src/streams/internal/async_promise.zig`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No unsafe casts between void and non-void return types
- [ ] `onSettleCtx` works correctly for fire-and-forget handlers
- [ ] All existing tests pass
- [ ] No segfaults in stream operations

return try internal.some_field.clone\(instance.ctx.allocator\)\;

title: Enable worker test result messages to main thread
description:
## Overview

Worker tests execute successfully but results are not communicated back to the main thread. This causes 7/14 console tests to show as errors \(0 subtests from worker context\).

## Current State

- Workers load and execute scripts correctly \(importScripts working\)
- testharness.js runs in worker context
- Tests execute in worker
- **BUT** test results are not posted back to main thread
- Main thread times out waiting for results

## Root Cause

Message dispatch in `message_channel.zig` was disabled \(lines 258-261 commented out\) to avoid cross-isolate V8 crashes. Immediate dispatch from worker isolate was causing issues.

## Technical Approach

Need to enable proper message queuing and dispatching:

1. **Queue messages in worker** - Worker's postMessage should queue, not dispatch immediately
2. **Process queue after control returns to main** - Main thread event loop processes queued messages
3. **Dispatch MessageEvent** - Create MessageEvent and invoke onmessage handler

## Files to Modify

1. **`src/html/workers/message_channel.zig`**
   - Re-enable message dispatch with proper queuing
   - Ensure messages are processed on correct isolate

2. **`src/webidl/impls/Worker.zig`**
   - `dispatchMessageEvent` exists but may not be triggered
   - Verify handleMessageFromWorkerCallback is called

3. **`src/html/worker_v8_context.zig`**
   - `workerPostMessageCallback` sends messages
   - May need to queue rather than immediate dispatch

## Event Loop Integration

The testharness.js in worker posts messages like:
```javascript
{ type: "result", status: 0, name: "test name", message: null }
{ type: "complete", tests: [...] }
```

These need to arrive at `fetch_tests_from_worker\(\)` on main thread.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. [ ] Worker postMessage queues message properly
2. [ ] Main thread receives queued messages
3. [ ] onmessage handler is invoked with MessageEvent
4. [ ] MessageEvent.data contains deserialized message
5. [ ] testharness.js receives worker test results

title: V8/Feature Limitations Analysis and Resolution
description:
## Overview

Analysis of 4 WebIDL WPT test failures caused by V8 API limitations or missing feature implementations.

---

## Issue 1: Legacy Factory Function Builtin Properties \(1 failure\)

**Test File:** `tests/wpt/webidl/ecmascript-binding/legacy-factory-function-builtin-properties.window.js`

**What the test expects:**
```javascript
const ownPropKeys = Reflect.ownKeys\(Image\).slice\(0, 3\)\;
assert_array_equals\(ownPropKeys, ["length", "name", "prototype"]\)\;
```

The test expects legacy factory functions \(like `Image`\) to have property enumeration order of exactly `["length", "name", "prototype"]` as the first three properties.

**Why it currently fails:**
V8's `FunctionTemplate` creates functions that include legacy `arguments` and `caller` accessor properties. These are non-configurable and cannot be deleted. The current code in `src/runtime/engines/v8/interface.zig:394-405` attempts to delete them but fails:

```zig
// Note: Per WebIDL spec, interface constructors should not have legacy
// "arguments" and "caller" properties. However, V8's FunctionTemplate creates
// functions with these as non-configurable accessor properties that cannot be
// deleted. This is a V8 limitation - we attempt deletion but it will fail.
```

**Root Cause:** **V8 API limitation** - Functions created via `FunctionTemplate` always have `arguments` and `caller` as non-configurable accessors.

**Can it be fixed?** 
- **Partial:** Using `v8_FunctionTemplate_RemovePrototype\(\)` removes prototype but not arguments/caller
- **Full fix:** Requires V8 internal API access or creating constructor functions via JavaScript code execution instead of FunctionTemplate API
- **Workaround:** Could create constructor as a regular function object using `v8.v8_Function_New\(\)` with careful prototype chain setup, but loses FunctionTemplate benefits \(signature checking, internal fields\)

**Implementation Approach:**
1. Create constructors using JavaScript evaluation for spec-compliant property order
2. Or accept as V8 limitation and document/skip test

---

## Issue 2: DOMException Error.isError \(1 failure\)

**Test File:** `tests/wpt/webidl/ecmascript-binding/es-exceptions/DOMException-is-error.any.js`

**What the test expects:**
```javascript
assert_true\(Error.isError\(new DOMException\(\)\)\)\;
```

**Why it currently fails:**
`Error.isError\(\)` is a TC39 Stage 3 proposal \(https://github.com/tc39/proposal-is-error\). It checks for an internal `[[ErrorData]]` slot that only native Error objects have.

**Root Cause:** **V8 feature limitation** - `Error.isError` is not yet available in V8. This proposal was at Stage 3 as of late 2024 and requires V8 to implement the feature.

**Current DOMException setup \(from `interface_bindings.zig:396-433`\):**
- `DOMException.prototype.__proto__ = Error.prototype` \(correctly set\)
- This makes `new DOMException\(\) instanceof Error === true`
- But `Error.isError\(\)` checks internal slots, not prototype chain

**Can it be fixed?**
- **NO** - This requires V8 engine support for the TC39 proposal
- The feature must be implemented in V8 itself to expose `Error.isError\(\)` and set the `[[ErrorData]]` slot

**Implementation Approach:**
1. Wait for V8 to ship `Error.isError` \(already Stage 3\)
2. Test is correctly written per spec, our implementation is correct
3. Mark test as expected failure until V8 ships the feature

---

## Issue 3: ObservableArray No Leak of Internals \(1 failure\)

**Test File:** `tests/wpt/webidl/ecmascript-binding/observable-array-no-leak-of-internals.window.js`

**What the test expects:**
```javascript
const observableArray = document.adoptedStyleSheets\;
let leaked_target = null\;
let leaked_handler = null\;

let target_leaker = \(target\) =\> { leaked_target = target\; return null\; }\;
Object.defineProperty\(Object.prototype, "getPrototypeOf", {get: function\(\) {
    leaked_handler = this\;
    return target_leaker\;
}}\)
Object.getPrototypeOf\(observableArray\)\;

assert_equals\(leaked_target, null, "The proxy target leaked."\)\;
assert_equals\(leaked_handler, null, "The proxy handler leaked."\)\;
```

**Why it currently fails:**
The test verifies that ObservableArray's internal proxy implementation doesn't leak its target or handler objects when `Object.getPrototypeOf` is called. Per WebIDL spec, ObservableArray is an "exotic object" backed by a Proxy with special invariants.

**Current implementation \(from `observable_arrays.zig`\):**
- Only provides Zig-side backing storage with change handlers
- Does NOT implement the JavaScript Proxy exotic object
- Comments explicitly state "The exotic object/Proxy wrapper will be added when V8 integration is ready"

**Root Cause:** **Missing implementation** - ObservableArray exotic object/Proxy not yet implemented in V8 bindings.

**Can it be fixed?** **YES**

**Implementation Approach:**
1. Create V8 Proxy object for ObservableArray backing
2. Implement Proxy handler with proper traps that don't leak internals:
   - `getPrototypeOf` trap must not expose handler
   - `[[Get]]`, `[[Set]]`, `[[Delete]]` traps for array operations
3. Use V8's `v8::Proxy::New\(\)` API
4. Wire to existing `ObservableArray\<T\>` backing storage
5. Ensure handler object is not accessible via prototype pollution attacks

---

## Issue 4: ObservableArray OwnKeys \(1 failure\)

**Test File:** `tests/wpt/webidl/ecmascript-binding/observable-array-ownkeys.window.js`

**What the test expects:**
```javascript
const observableArray = document.adoptedStyleSheets\;
// Initially only "length"
assert_array_equals\(Object.getOwnPropertyNames\(observableArray\), ["length"]\)\;

// After adding string properties
observableArray["zzz"] = true\;
observableArray["aaa"] = true\;
assert_array_equals\(Object.getOwnPropertyNames\(observableArray\), ["length", "zzz", "aaa"]\)\;

// After adding indexed properties
observableArray[0] = new CSSStyleSheet\(\)\;
observableArray[1] = new CSSStyleSheet\(\)\;
assert_array_equals\(Object.getOwnPropertyNames\(observableArray\), ["0", "1", "length", "zzz", "aaa"]\)\;

// Symbol properties work correctly
observableArray[Symbol.toStringTag] = "string_tag"\;
assert_array_equals\(Object.getOwnPropertySymbols\(observableArray\), [Symbol.toStringTag, Symbol.toPrimitive]\)\;
```

**Why it currently fails:**
Same root cause as Issue 3 - the ObservableArray exotic object's `[[OwnPropertyKeys]]` internal method is not implemented.

**Root Cause:** **Missing implementation** - ObservableArray Proxy's `ownKeys` trap not implemented.

**Can it be fixed?** **YES** \(same fix as Issue 3\)

**Implementation Approach:**
1. Implement `ownKeys` Proxy trap that returns keys in correct order:
   - Array indices first \(numeric, ascending\)
   - Then "length"
   - Then other string keys \(insertion order\)
   - Symbol keys via separate trap
2. This is part of the same ObservableArray exotic object implementation as Issue 3

---

## Summary Table

\| Issue \| Test \| Root Cause \| Fixable? \| Priority \|
\|-------\|------\|------------\|----------\|----------\|
\| 1 \| legacy-factory-function-builtin-properties \| V8 FunctionTemplate limitation \| Partial \(workaround\) \| P2 \|
\| 2 \| DOMException-is-error \| TC39 proposal not in V8 yet \| NO \(V8 dependency\) \| P3 \|
\| 3 \| observable-array-no-leak-of-internals \| ObservableArray Proxy not implemented \| YES \| P1 \|
\| 4 \| observable-array-ownkeys \| ObservableArray Proxy not implemented \| YES \| P1 \|

## Recommended Priority

1. **Issues 3 \& 4 \(ObservableArray\)** - Can be fixed together by implementing Proxy-based exotic object
2. **Issue 1 \(Legacy Factory\)** - Workaround possible but complex, may accept as V8 limitation
3. **Issue 2 \(Error.isError\)** - Wait for V8 to implement TC39 proposal

description:
## Problem

The WPT runner crashes with "Bus error" when running the second test file. The first test completes, but when the second test tries to register interfaces, V8 crashes due to stale template cache pointers.

## Root Cause Analysis

Three independent agents performed triple-pass root cause analysis and converged on:

1. **Primary Issue**: V8Interface caches function templates in comptime-generated static variables. When isolate is disposed, these pointers become dangling.

2. **Secondary Issue**: Additional Zig-side globals are NOT being cleared on isolate disposal:
   -  in engine.zig
   -  in namespace.zig
   - Thread-local DOM state (reactions, mutation observers)

3. **Architectural Issue**: No central isolate lifecycle manager - cleanup is scattered and incomplete.

## Solution Strategy

**Phase 1**: Immediate fix - clear missing globals to stop the crash
**Phase 2**: Correct architecture - isolate-local template storage using V8's embedder data slots
**Phase 3**: Future-proofing - cleanup registry for automatic participation

## Success Criteria

- [ ] WPT runner can execute multiple test files without crashing
- [ ] No use-after-free or memory corruption on isolate disposal
- [ ] Templates properly scoped to isolate lifetime
- [ ] Clear documentation for adding new V8-dependent state

- Blocks: whatwg-lv6ig (CookieStore WPT integration)

title: Audit and document WebIDL type mappings for object/symbol
description:
## Task

Audit and document the WebIDL type mappings where `object` and `symbol` map to `*anyopaque`.

## Current Mapping

```zig
// tests/webidl/type_metadata_test.zig:92, 99
try testing.expectEqual\(*anyopaque, meta.zig_type\)\;  // for object
try testing.expectEqual\(*anyopaque, meta.zig_type\)\;  // for symbol
```

## Analysis

Per WebIDL spec:
- `object` - Any ECMAScript object \(not a primitive\)
- `symbol` - ECMAScript Symbol

These map to `*anyopaque` because they represent any JS object, not a specific type.

## Questions to Answer

1. Is `*anyopaque` the best representation?
2. Could we use a tagged union for common object types?
3. Should we have `JSObject` and `JSSymbol` wrapper types?

## Proposed Enhancement

```zig
pub const JSObject = struct {
    ptr: *anyopaque,  // KEEP: anyopaque required for JS object reference
    
    pub fn isArray\(self: JSObject\) bool { ... }
    pub fn isFunction\(self: JSObject\) bool { ... }
}\;

pub const JSSymbol = struct {
    ptr: *anyopaque,  // KEEP: anyopaque required for JS symbol reference
    pub fn description\(self: JSSymbol\) ?[]const u8 { ... }
}\;
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Document why object/symbol use anyopaque
- [ ] Add KEEP comments with clear reasoning
- [ ] Consider typed wrappers if beneficial
- [ ] Update tests to verify type safety where possible

title: 1.1.1: Implement HTML Event Loop Core
description:
# Implement HTML Event Loop Core

## Spec Reference
HTML Standard Section 8.1.7 "Event loops"

## Location
`src/html/event_loop/event_loop.zig`

## Requirements

### Data Structures
```zig
pub const EventLoop = struct {
    allocator: Allocator,
    task_queues: TaskQueueSet,
    microtask_queue: MicrotaskQueue,
    currently_running_task: ?*Task,
    performing_microtask_checkpoint: bool,
    
    // Platform integration
    platform: *PlatformTimerBackend,
    
    // Rendering
    last_render_time: i64,
    needs_rendering: bool,
};
```

### Core Algorithm: Processing Model
Per spec section 8.1.7.3:
1. Let oldestTask be null
2. Let taskStartTime be current high resolution time
3. If task queue has runnable task:
   - Let oldestTask be first runnable task
   - Remove from queue
   - Set currently running task to oldestTask
   - Perform oldestTask's steps
   - Set currently running task to null
4. Perform a microtask checkpoint
5. Update the rendering (if needed)
6. If no tasks, wait for task or timeout

### Methods to Implement
- `pub fn spin(self: *EventLoop) void` - Main processing model
- `pub fn queueTask(self: *EventLoop, source: TaskSource, steps: TaskSteps) void`
- `pub fn queueMicrotask(self: *EventLoop, callback: MicrotaskCallback) void`
- `pub fn performMicrotaskCheckpoint(self: *EventLoop) void`
- `pub fn shouldRender(self: *EventLoop) bool`

### Integration Points
- Must integrate with PlatformTimerBackend for sleep/wake
- Must support mock time for testing
- Must handle nested event loops (for alert/confirm/prompt)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tasks execute in FIFO order per queue
- [ ] Microtasks all drain before next task
- [ ] Rendering step called at appropriate intervals
- [ ] No busy-waiting when idle
- [ ] All memory properly freed on deinit

## Test Cases
1. Queue single task, verify execution
2. Queue multiple tasks same source, verify FIFO
3. Queue microtask during task, verify runs before next task
4. Microtask queues another microtask, verify all drain
5. Test with mock time backend
6. Test memory cleanup

# Implement HTML Tokenizer

## Spec Reference

## Location
`src/html/parser/tokenizer.zig`

## Requirements

### Tokenizer State Machine
Implement all 80 states from spec:
```zig
pub const State = enum {
    // Data states

    rcdata_end_tag_name,
    rawtext_less_than_sign,
    rawtext_end_tag_open,
    rawtext_end_tag_name,

```

### Token Types
```zig
pub const Token = union(enum) {
    doctype: DoctypeToken,
    start_tag: TagToken,
    end_tag: TagToken,
    comment: CommentToken,
    character: u21, // Unicode code point
    eof: void,
};

pub const DoctypeToken = struct {
    name: ?[]const u8,
    public_identifier: ?[]const u8,
    system_identifier: ?[]const u8,
    force_quirks: bool,
};

pub const TagToken = struct {
    name: []const u8,
    attributes: ArrayList(Attribute),
    self_closing: bool,
};

pub const Attribute = struct {
    name: []const u8,
    value: []const u8,
};

pub const CommentToken = struct {
    data: []const u8,
};
```

### Tokenizer Structure
```zig
pub const Tokenizer = struct {
    allocator: Allocator,
    input: []const u8,
    position: usize,
    state: State,
    return_state: State,
    
    // Current token being built
    current_token: ?Token,
    current_tag_name: ArrayList(u8),
    current_attribute_name: ArrayList(u8),
    current_attribute_value: ArrayList(u8),
    current_comment_data: ArrayList(u8),
    current_doctype: DoctypeToken,
    
    // Temporary buffer for various uses
    temporary_buffer: ArrayList(u8),
    
    // Character reference
    character_reference_code: u32,
    
    // Last emitted start tag (for appropriate end tag matching)
    last_start_tag_name: ?[]const u8,
    
    // Error callback
    error_callback: ?*const fn(ParseError) void,
    
    pub fn init(allocator: Allocator, input: []const u8) Tokenizer;
    pub fn next(self: *Tokenizer) ?Token;
    pub fn setState(self: *Tokenizer, state: State) void;
    
    // Internal state machine
    fn processState(self: *Tokenizer, char: u21) ?Token;
};
```

### Character Reference Handling
Include named character references table (~2,000 entries):
```zig
// src/html/parser/entities.zig
pub const named_character_references = std.ComptimeStringMap([]const u21, .{
    .{ "AElig", &.{0xC6} },
    .{ "AElig;", &.{0xC6} },
    .{ "AMP", &.{0x26} },
    .{ "AMP;", &.{0x26} },
    // ... ~2000 more entries
});
```

Fix Event subclass memory leaks - missing parent deinit calls
description:
## Problem

Event subclass impl files were not calling `interfaces.Event.deinit\(instance\)` in their `deinit` functions, causing memory leaks of the `state.base.own.type` DOMString which is cloned in constructors.

## Fixed \(Manual\)

The following fully-implemented Event subclasses have been fixed:
- ✅ ErrorEvent.zig
- ✅ MessageEvent.zig  
- ✅ ProgressEvent.zig
- ✅ CloseEvent.zig
- ✅ CustomEvent.zig

## Not Fixed \(Stub Files\)

~100 Event subclass stub files don't call parent deinit, but they also don't allocate anything \(constructor params are discarded with `_ = @"type"`\). These don't need fixing until they're fully implemented.

## Root Cause

When Event subclasses clone `@"type".clone\(ctx.allocator\)` to `state.base.own.type`, the parent Event.deinit must be called to free it. The pattern is:

```zig
pub fn deinit\(instance: *runtime.Instance\) void {
    // Clean up subclass resources...
    
    // REQUIRED: Call parent deinit to clean up inherited resources
    interfaces.Event.deinit\(instance\)\;
}
```

## Verification

- Build passes: ✅
- All tests pass: ✅

title: Epic: Fix V8 Handle Lifetimes in Dictionary Conversion \(Production-Ready\)
description:
# Epic: Fix V8 Handle Lifetimes in Dictionary Conversion \(Production-Ready\)

## Problem Statement

When V8 converts JavaScript objects to Zig dictionaries, interface-typed members and callbacks are stored as raw `*const anyopaque` pointers via the `fromV8Value` function. These are actually `Local\<Value\>` handles that become **dangling pointers** after the HandleScope ends.

### Current Behavior \(BROKEN\)

```zig
// src/runtime/engines/v8/conversions.zig \(lines 928-938\)
if \(T == *const anyopaque\) {
    // Returns raw Local pointer - becomes DANGLING after HandleScope ends\!
    return @ptrCast\(value\)\;
}
```

### Crash Sequence

1. JavaScript calls `readable.pipeThrough\(transformStream\)`
2. `fromV8Value` extracts `transform.writable` as `*const anyopaque` \(raw Local\)
3. Constructor HandleScope ends
4. The Local handle is now **INVALID**
5. Later code tries to create Global from invalid Local → **SEGFAULT at 0x8**

### Crash Location

```
Segmentation fault at address 0x8
v8_Value_ToGlobal \(v8_wrapper.cpp\)
  → global_handles.zig:68 in create
  → algorithm.zig:151 in jsCallbackAlgorithmGlobal
  → ReadableStream.zig:2063 in setUpReadableStreamDefaultController
```

## Solution: Option A - Fix at Conversion Layer

Fix the problem once at the source in `conversions.zig`. When extracting values that need to persist beyond HandleScope \(functions, objects\), create Global handles immediately.

### Why Option A is Best

\| Aspect \| Option A \(conversions.zig\) \| Option B \(each impl\) \|
\|--------\|---------------------------\|---------------------\|
\| Code changes \| 1 place \| 3+ stream impls \|
\| Future-proof \| ✅ Yes \| ❌ Must remember \|
\| Memory management \| Need cleanup tracking \| Same \|
\| Architectural \| ✅ Correct boundary \| ❌ Leaky abstraction \|

### Implementation Approach

```zig
// In conversions.zig
if \(T == *const anyopaque\) {
    // Check if this is a function/object that needs to persist beyond HandleScope
    if \(ffi.v8_Value_IsFunction\(value\) or ffi.v8_Value_IsObject\(value\)\) {
        // Create a Global handle so it survives after this scope
        if \(ffi.v8_Value_ToGlobal\(isolate, value\)\) \|global\| {
            return @ptrCast\(global\)\;
        }
    }
    // For primitives, the value can be returned as-is \(or extracted\)
    return @ptrCast\(value\)\;
}
```

### Memory Management Strategy

Use **weak Global handles** that V8 can GC when JavaScript no longer references the object:
- V8 automatically cleans them up
- Matches JavaScript semantics
- No manual disposal required
- Prevents memory leaks

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All `*const anyopaque` function/object values converted to Global handles
- [ ] Global handles use weak semantics for automatic GC cleanup
- [ ] No segfaults when running `pipeThrough` or similar operations
- [ ] WPT test `encoding/streams/decode-bad-chunks.any.js` passes
- [ ] No memory leaks \(verify with ASAN\)
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass

## Files to Modify

1. **Primary**: `src/runtime/engines/v8/conversions.zig` - Core fix
2. **FFI**: `src/runtime/engines/v8/v8_wrapper.cpp` - Add weak handle support
3. **FFI**: `src/runtime/engines/v8/ffi.zig` - Declare weak handle functions
4. **Support**: `src/runtime/engines/v8/global_handles.zig` - Add weak handle wrapper

## Testing Strategy

1. Unit test: Verify Global handles created for functions/objects
2. Unit test: Verify primitives don't create Global handles
3. Integration test: `pipeThrough` receives valid `*runtime.Instance`
4. WPT test: `encoding/streams/decode-bad-chunks.any.js` passes
5. Memory test: Run with ASAN, verify no leaks

## Estimated Effort

- **Total**: 2-3 days
- **Subtasks**: 6

## Related Issues

- Supersedes: whatwg-xurhe \(incorrectly closed as obsolete\)
- Related: whatwg-csriw \(V8 Handle Lifecycle epic\)
- Related: whatwg-e702t \(Global handle FFI - may already exist\)
- Blocks: WPT test suite progress

title: Fix WPT Runner Hang After ~10 Tests
description:
## Problem Summary
The WPT runner hangs after ~10 tests when running a full directory \(270+ tests\) at 100% CPU. Three independent investigations identified multiple interconnected root causes.

## Root Causes Identified

### PRIMARY: `poll\(\)` Returns Wrong Value \(CRITICAL\)
- Location: `src/runtime/engines/v8/libuv_timer.zig:190-197`
- `uv_run\(\)` returns count of active handles, not whether callbacks were invoked
- Causes event loop to spin at 100% CPU without yielding

### SECONDARY: Timer Handle Accumulation \(HIGH\)
- Location: `tests/wpt_runner/browser_context.zig:1362-1374`
- `clearTimerInterface\(\)` destroys V8TimerContext but NOT underlying libuv timer handles
- Orphaned handles persist between tests

### TERTIARY: Cleanup Uses Wrong UV Mode \(HIGH\)
- Location: `src/runtime/engines/v8/libuv_timer.zig:94-110`
- `UV_RUN_NOWAIT` may not process close callbacks during deinit
- Timer handles may not be properly closed

### QUATERNARY: Global Registry Uses `page_allocator` \(LOW\)
- Location: `src/runtime/internal_state.zig:53-62`
- May cause memory fragmentation over many test cycles

## Success Criteria
- WPT runner completes 270+ dom/nodes tests without hanging
- CPU usage stays reasonable during test execution
- No timer handle leaks between tests

## Files to Modify
- `src/runtime/engines/v8/libuv_timer.zig`
- `tests/wpt_runner/browser_context.zig`
- `src/runtime/internal_state.zig`
- `src/runtime/root.zig`

comments.text:
Architecture analysis completed:

## Current Problem
External code \(e.g., `src/html/script_execution.zig`\) imports impls directly to access internal state functions like `hasAlreadyStarted\(\)`, `setAlreadyStarted\(\)`, etc.

## Correct Architecture

1. **Create internal module** \(e.g., `src/html/script_element_internals.zig`\):
   - Defines state structure
   - Defines internal operations \(hasAlreadyStarted, setAlreadyStarted, etc.\)
   - Uses a registry pattern for state storage

2. **Modify impl** \(e.g., `src/webidl/impls/HTMLScriptElement.zig`\):
   - Imports the internal module
   - Delegates internal state operations to it
   - Keeps only WebIDL bindings \(init, deinit, get_*, set_*, call_*\)

3. **Update external code** \(e.g., `src/html/script_execution.zig`\):
   - Imports internal module instead of impl
   - Calls `script_element_internals.hasAlreadyStarted\(\)` instead of `HTMLScriptElementImpl.hasAlreadyStarted\(\)`

## Challenge
This requires:
1. Adding internal modules to build.zig with proper import relationships
2. The internal module needs access to `runtime.Instance` which comes from the runtime package
3. Careful ordering to avoid circular dependencies

## Recommended Approach
Start with one interface \(HTMLScriptElement\) as a proof of concept, then apply the pattern to others.

## Files to create for HTMLScriptElement migration:
- `src/html/script_element_internals.zig` - state and internal ops
- Update `src/html/root.zig` - export new module
- Update `src/webidl/impls/HTMLScriptElement.zig` - delegate to internal
- Update `src/html/script_execution.zig` - use internal module

Fix from_iterable_algorithm.zig error-to-anyopaque casts
description:
## Summary

from_iterable_algorithm.zig casts Zig error values to `*anyopaque` which is fundamentally broken - error values are not pointers.

## Current Code \(from_iterable_algorithm.zig:78-81\)

```zig
const next_result = iter_record.next\(\) catch \|err\| {
    const err_ptr: *const anyopaque = @ptrCast\(\&err\)\;
    ReadableStreamDefaultController.call_error\(controller, 
        webidl.Opt\(runtime.JSValue\).passed\(runtime.JSValue.fromAnyopaque\(err_ptr\)\)\) catch {}\;
```

This pattern appears 5 times in the file and is CRITICALLY WRONG because:
1. `err` is a stack-allocated error union value, not a heap pointer
2. Taking `\&err` creates a dangling pointer once the catch block exits
3. Casting error to anyopaque loses all error information
4. `fromAnyopaque` treats it as a V8 handle which it is not

## Solution

Create proper error-to-JSValue conversion:

```zig
const next_result = iter_record.next\(\) catch \|err\| {
    // Create a proper JS error value
    const error_value = runtime.JSValue.createError\(
        allocator,
        @errorName\(err\),
    \)\;
    ReadableStreamDefaultController.call_error\(controller, 
        webidl.Opt\(runtime.JSValue\).passed\(error_value\)\) catch {}\;
```

Or use webidl.errors.Exception:

```zig
const exception = try webidl.errors.Exception.fromZigError\(allocator, err\)\;
// Pass exception through proper error channel
```

## Files to Modify

- `src/streams/internal/from_iterable_algorithm.zig` - All 5 occurrences

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No error-to-anyopaque casts
- [ ] Proper error propagation to JS
- [ ] No dangling pointers
- [ ] Tests pass
